_authority: Canonical token set for a course module's visual layer. MEASURED from the reference module, not retyped. The guide points here; change a value here and everything follows.
_rule: Module 1's :root is the reference. Never hardcode a colour, radius, shadow or font outside this block.
_modes: A slide is light by default, dark when it carries .dark or .photo. Tokens ending -l are for light slides, -d for dark. Pick by the surface behind the element.

--blue.role: the live accent - links, active state, focus

--blue2.role: a softer blue for secondary marks

--amber.role: the one emphasis colour - takeaway rule, key figure

--amber-ink.role: text ON an amber wash, where amber itself would not pass contrast

--ink.role: body text on a light slide

--deep-2.role: raised surface on a dark slide (cards)

--txt-d.role: body text on a dark slide

--blue-wash-d.role: blue tint behind content, dark slide

--blue-wash-l.role: blue tint behind content, light slide

--amber-wash-d.role: amber tint behind content, dark slide

--amber-wash-l.role: amber tint behind content, light slide

--cold.role: cold / cryogenic - a course-content colour, not a UI state

--mono.role: figures, codes, anything that must line up

--good-wash-l.role: ground behind a correct answer or a passed check
--good-wash-l.added: 2.2.0 - three files had hand-rolled it (task.css --okbg, gb_page .crit, ETPA1)

--warn-wash-l.role: ground behind a wrong answer or a hard stop

--on-blue.role: text and icons ON a filled --blue surface
--on-blue.added: 2.2.0 - was hard-coded five times in the golden deck

--on-navy.role: secondary text ON a filled --navy surface

aliases._note: A second dialect exists in shipped modules 03, 05 and 06. These names mean the same thing. Read them; do not write them.

open_questions.hazard_colours: Modules 03/05/06 declare --red, --flame and --toxic. The reference set has no hazard colours at all, which is a real gap for a gas course. Adding them is an owner decision - do not invent values.
